releases.name: v1.1.0
releases.body:
### Highlights
- **Startup splash screen** (new `SplashWindow`): starts Ollama, picks a default model by detected VRAM, downloads it with a live progress bar, preloads it into GPU/VRAM, then opens the editor.
- **Cursor V2-style dark UI**: new `Styles/Colors.axaml` + `Controls.axaml` design tokens applied across the main window, editor, panels, file explorer, terminal, settings, and marketplace.
- **Performance & memory pass** across indexing, reversing, editor, and file-system subsystems.

### Models / Provisioning
- VRAM-based default selection (threshold 20 GB):
  - High-VRAM → `its_the_jisoo/qwen3.6-27B-uncensored-hauhaucs-aggressive:latest`
  - Low-VRAM → `fredrezones55/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Uncensored-HauhauCS-Aggressive:IQ2_M`
- One-time provisioning tracked via new `DefaultModelEnsured` preference.
- **Verify-after-pull**: provisioning is marked complete only after the model is confirmed in `ollama list` (a completed stream is no longer treated as success).
- **Self-healing**: a missing model is re-downloaded even if the flag is set; stale/never-installed selections are cleared.
- Tag-tolerant matching normalizes an implicit `:latest`.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A local, AI-powered IDE featuring integrated decompilation and reverse engineering tools.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: LibreCode is a local-first coding environment and reverse engineering toolkit built with Avalonia UI. It deeply integrates with local Ollama instances to provide autonomous coding agents, codebase indexing via RAG, and inline code completion without sending data to external APIs. Beyond standard IDE features, it includes a comprehensive reverse engineering suite capable of decompiling and debugging .NET assemblies, WebAssembly (WASM), and native ELF binaries. The system explicitly focuses on static analysis, obfuscation detection, and anti-debugging evasion, making it a unique hybrid of an AI coding assistant and a security analysis tool.
keyFeatures: Local AI integration: Leverages local Ollama models for code generation, autonomous agent workflows, and codebase RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation).
.NET decompilation: Integrates the ILSpy engine to browse decompiled C# source code, inspect PE metadata, and simulate IL bytecode execution.
WebAssembly toolkit: Provides zero-dependency WAT disassembly, live CDP debugging, and a step-through interpreter for analyzing WASM binaries.
Native ELF analysis: Disassembles x86/ARM binaries, extracts dynamic symbols, and statically flags Obfuscator-LLVM artifacts like control-flow flattening.
Anti-debugging evasion: Scans modules for host environment checks and automatically generates Harmony patches or bypass playbooks to stay invisible.
Harmony patch generator: Instantly generates ready-to-compile HarmonyLib patches directly from decompiled .NET methods.

useCases.title: Local AI-assisted coding
useCases.description: Developers working in air-gapped or highly secure environments can utilize autonomous coding agents using locally hosted Ollama models.

useCases.title: Malware analysis
useCases.description: Security researchers can safely decompile and interpret obfuscated .NET or WASM payloads locally to analyze their control flow without executing them.

useCases.title: Game modding
useCases.description: Mod developers can inspect game binaries, find target methods, and automatically generate Harmony patches to modify behavior.

useCases.title: Vulnerability detection
useCases.description: Engineers can send disassembled ELF or WASM functions directly to the local AI to identify security flaws and purpose identification.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: LibreCode is designed for security researchers, reverse engineers, game modders, and privacy-conscious developers who need deep local binary analysis combined with offline AI assistance.
